# Embedded C++ - Wikipedia

> ## Excerpt
> From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

---
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

**Embedded C++** (**EC++**) is a [dialect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_language_dialect "Programming language dialect") of the [C++](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C++ "C++") programming language for [embedded systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedded_system "Embedded system"). It was defined by an industry group led by major Japanese [central processing unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_processing_unit "Central processing unit") (CPU) manufacturers, including [NEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NEC_Corporation "NEC Corporation"), [Hitachi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hitachi,_Ltd. "Hitachi, Ltd."), [Fujitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujitsu "Fujitsu"), and [Toshiba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toshiba "Toshiba"), to address the shortcomings of C++ for embedded applications. The goal of the effort<sup about="#mwt4" id="cite_ref-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-1&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedded_C%2B%2B#cite_note-1" id="mwDg"><span id="mwDw"><span id="mwEA">[</span>1<span id="mwEQ">]</span></span></a></sup> is to preserve the most useful [object-oriented](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object-oriented_programming "Object-oriented programming") features of the C++ language yet minimize code size while maximizing execution efficiency and making [compiler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compiler "Compiler") construction simpler. The official website states the goal as "to provide embedded systems programmers with a subset of C++ that is easy for the average C programmer to understand and use".<sup about="#mwt5" id="cite_ref-qa_2-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;qa&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-qa-2&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedded_C%2B%2B#cite_note-qa-2" id="mwFA"><span id="mwFQ"><span id="mwFg">[</span>2<span id="mwFw">]</span></span></a></sup>

Embedded C++ excludes some features of C++.

| Feature | ISO/ANSI C C++ | Embedded C++ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Exception handling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exception_handling "Exception handling") | ![Yes](data:image/png;base64,) | ![No](data:image/png;base64,) |
| [Multiple inheritance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_inheritance "Multiple inheritance") | ![Yes](data:image/png;base64,) | ![No](data:image/png;base64,) |
| `mutable`, a [storage class specifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storage_class_specifier "Storage class specifier") | ![Yes](data:image/png;base64,) | ![No](data:image/png;base64,) |
| [Namespaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namespaces "Namespaces") | ![Yes](data:image/png;base64,) | ![No](data:image/png;base64,) |
| [Templates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generic_programming#Templates_in_C++ "Generic programming") | ![Yes](data:image/png;base64,) | ![No](data:image/png;base64,) |
| [Run-time type information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Run-time_type_information "Run-time type information") (`typeid`) | ![Yes](data:image/png;base64,) | ![No](data:image/png;base64,) |
| Style casts  
(`static_cast`, `dynamic_cast`, `reinterpret_cast`, and `const_cast`) | ![Yes](data:image/png;base64,) | ![No](data:image/png;base64,) |
| [Virtual base classes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_base_class "Virtual base class") | ![Yes](data:image/png;base64,) | ![No](data:image/png;base64,) |

Some compilers, such as those from Green Hills and IAR Systems, allow certain features of ISO/ANSI C++ to be enabled in Embedded C++. [IAR Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAR_Systems "IAR Systems") calls this "Extended Embedded C++".<sup about="#mwt44" id="cite_ref-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-3&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedded_C%2B%2B#cite_note-3" id="mwYQ"><span id="mwYg"><span id="mwYw">[</span>3<span id="mwZA">]</span></span></a></sup>

An EC++ program can be compiled with any C++ compiler. But, a compiler specific to EC++ may have an easier time doing optimization.

Compilers specific to EC++ are provided by companies such as:

-   [IAR Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAR_Systems "IAR Systems")<sup about="#mwt47" id="cite_ref-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-4&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedded_C%2B%2B#cite_note-4" id="mwaw"><span id="mwbA"><span id="mwbQ">[</span>4<span id="mwbg">]</span></span></a></sup>
-   [Freescale Semiconductor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freescale_Semiconductor "Freescale Semiconductor"), (spin-off from [Motorola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorola "Motorola") in 2004 who had acquired [Metrowerks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrowerks "Metrowerks") in 1999)
-   Tasking Software,<sup about="#mwt50" id="cite_ref-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-5&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedded_C%2B%2B#cite_note-5" id="mwdA"><span id="mwdQ"><span id="mwdg">[</span>5<span id="mwdw">]</span></span></a></sup> part of [Altium Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altium_Limited "Altium Limited")
-   [Green Hills Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Hills_Software "Green Hills Software")<sup about="#mwt53" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-6&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedded_C%2B%2B#cite_note-6" id="mwew"><span id="mwfA"><span id="mwfQ">[</span>6<span id="mwfg">]</span></span></a></sup>

The language has had a poor reception with many expert C++ programmers. In particular, [Bjarne Stroustrup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bjarne_Stroustrup "Bjarne Stroustrup") says, "To the best of my knowledge EC++ is dead (2004), and if it isn't it ought to be."<sup about="#mwt58" id="cite_ref-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-7&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedded_C%2B%2B#cite_note-7" id="mwgw"><span id="mwhA"><span id="mwhQ">[</span>7<span id="mwhg">]</span></span></a></sup> In fact, the official English EC++ website has not been updated since 2002. Nevertheless, a restricted subset of C++ (based on Embedded C++) has been adopted by [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") as the exclusive programming language to create all [I/O Kit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XNU#IOKit "XNU") device drivers for Apple's macOS, iPadOS and iOS operating systems of the popular Macintosh, iPhone, and iPad products.<sup about="#mwt61" id="cite_ref-8" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-8&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedded_C%2B%2B#cite_note-8" id="mwiQ"><span id="mwig"><span id="mwiw">[</span>8<span id="mwjA">]</span></span></a></sup> Apple engineers felt the exceptions, multiple inheritance, templates, and runtime type information features of standard C++ were either insufficient or not efficient enough for use in a high-performance, multithreaded kernel.<sup about="#mwt64" id="cite_ref-9" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-9&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedded_C%2B%2B#cite_note-9" id="mwjQ"><span id="mwjg"><span id="mwjw">[</span>9<span id="mwkA">]</span></span></a></sup>
